How to play Design Thinking Quest

The game turns Class 10 into five missions. Each mission starts with a real problem from Team Menu, breaks it down to what is certainly true, and then lets you learn, read the slides with their notes, build, check yourself and explain the idea back. Everything from the class is inside: the lecture mapped to the slides, the flash-cards and quiz, the slides with notes, Lab 05 with its animation, and every link, video and abbreviation.

ControlWhat it does
🗺️ Mapback to the mission map
🔑 Vaultsearch all links, videos and abbreviations
❔ How to playthe rules in five lines
↺start again from zero (clears your progress in this browser)
XP baryour experience points (XP) and level; badges are counted next to it
Formative only: nothing in the game counts toward your grade and nothing leaves your browser.

1 · Open the game and choose a mission

Download the file DIG123_Class10_Design-Thinking_GAME_Design-Thinking-Quest.html and open it in any modern browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) — on a laptop, tablet or phone. No installation, no account, no internet needed.

The mission map shows Missions 1–4 (the four lessons of Class 10), Mission 5 (Lab 05), the Vault and the opening/closing slides. Missions can be played in any order; 1 → 5 is the recommended path.

Every mission starts with ① a real problem from Team Menu's Sprint 3. Choose the answer you think is right: the game tells you why, then lists what is certainly true — the building blocks of the method.

2 · Learn the lesson and read the slides with their notes

② Learn contains the full lesson: definitions, tables, the real-life example and the diagram. The dark chips (▶ Slide 10) tell you which slide of the deck covers each part.

Press I have read this lesson to collect the XP and move on.

③ Slides shows the lesson's slides one by one. Press 🗒️ Notes to read the speaker notes under each slide. Look at every slide once to complete the stage.

3 · Build: apply the idea with your own hands

④ Build is a hands-on challenge: place the five modes on the Double Diamond (Mission 1), sort interview notes into the empathy map (Mission 2), put ideas into the impact × feasibility grid (Mission 3), rank usability problems by severity × frequency (Mission 4).

Click an item, then click where it belongs (or choose from the list). Press Check: green rows are right, red rows need another try. You can retry as often as you like; the XP comes when everything is right.

4 · Flash-cards and the formative quiz

⑤ Cards: click each of the six cards to turn it. Say the definition aloud before you turn it — that is how the cards work best.

⑥ Quiz: six questions — four MCQ (Multiple-Choice Question, one right answer) and two MSQ (Multiple-Select Question) whose number of right answers is shown in round brackets. Use 💡 Hint if you are stuck; after Check, every option shows why it is right or wrong.

The quiz is formative: it does not count toward your grade and nothing is sent anywhere.

5 · Explain it back, earn badges, prepare Lab 05, search the Vault

⑦ Explain it back: write the idea of the mission in one sentence, as if a friend missed the class; then compare with the model sentence. If yours says the same in your words, claim the XP.

Finishing all seven stages gives a badge and pushes your level: Observer → Interviewer → Framer → Maker → Tester → Design Thinker.

Mission 5 shows the seven boxes of Lab 05 as an animation and the steps with their “Done when” checks. Tick each step once you understand what it asks.

🔑 Vault: type a word (for example HMW, severity or NN/g) to find every link, video and abbreviation of the class.

FAQ

  • Where is my progress saved? In this browser only. Another browser or device starts from zero; private windows forget it when closed.
  • Can I play on my phone? Yes — the layout adapts to small screens.
  • Do the external links work offline? No: videos and official sites need internet. Before opening one, apply the Link and Download Safety Checklist of the Legal Notice (Annex C).
  • Is the game required? No. It is a study aid for Class 10 and Lab 05; the Study Hub and the lecture page cover the same content.
  • Why “problem first”? Starting from a real problem, reducing it to what is certainly true and only then learning the tool you need is a well-known teaching principle — Elon Musk has described it as teaching “to the problem, not to the tools” for the school he created for his children.
